passage: Application for a special event permit, filed by the Windlass Rowing Club for the Head of the Darrow regatta, river miles 4 through 7 of the Darrow, second Saturday of October, 7 a.m. to 3 p.m. The applicant expects 380 competing crews in 14 divisions, racing in procession at 15 second intervals, with 2,000 spectators concentrated at the Pemble footbridge and the finish meadow. passage: Determination of wage claim, Office of Labor Standards, claim 19-4471, claimant Rufus Pemberton against Starling Scaffold Company. The claimant, employed as a yard foreman from March of last year until his discharge in January, claims unpaid overtime of 4,700 dollars for 214 hours worked beyond forty per week, relying on his own notebook records. The employer contends the claimant was an exempt supervisor ineligible for overtime, citing his title and his rate of 31 dollars hourly, the yard's highest. The examiner finds the exemption not established: the claimant spent, by the employer's own scheduling records, over 70 percent of his hours on loading and repair work indistinguishable from the yard crew's, directed the work of at most two helpers, and lacked authority to hire, discipline, or set rates, the qualifying duties under rule 20. The notebook, kept daily and corroborated at sampled dates by gate logs, is accepted as the more reliable record over the employer's reconstructed timesheets, prepared after the claim was filed. Award: 4,700 dollars in overtime, liquidated damages in the like amount as the statute directs absent good faith, and interest; total 9,704 dollars. The employer's counterclaim for an unreturned power drill, valued at 260 dollars, is outside this office's jurisdiction. Appeal lies within 21 days.
question: How many hours of unpaid overtime did the claimant claim?

passage: Application for certification as an organic producer, Bindweed Hollow Farm, submitted to the Meridian Certification Cooperative. The farm comprises 61 acres: 38 in mixed vegetables and small fruit, 15 in pasture for a laying flock of 400 hens, and 8 in woodlot and farmstead. The applicant documents the required three year transition for all cropland, the last conventional input, a synthetic fungicide on the strawberry block, having been applied in June three years and two months before the planned first certified harvest. Buffer zones of 30 feet separate cropland from the neighboring Klepper orchard, which sprays conventionally; the buffer harvest, sold as conventional at the farm stand, is tracked in a separate ledger sampled by the reviewer. Inputs listed for approval include compost from the farm's own windrows, fish emulsion, and an approved kaolin clay for the pear trees. Seed records show organic seed for 84 percent of varieties, with documented unavailability searches for the remainder, including the farm's signature paste tomato, Verrano, for which three suppliers were queried. The poultry section discloses one antibiotic treatment of an injured hen, removed from the certified flock and tagged, consistent with the humane treatment rule. Inspection is requested for August, before the onion harvest. Fees of 1,150 dollars are enclosed.
question: How many hens are in the laying flock?

passage: Notice of intended prosecution and stipulated settlement, Fisheries Enforcement Division, case F-2210, respondent the fishing vessel Tern's Reward, owner and master Silas Quandt. On July 22 a boarding at the Middle Bank grounds found aboard 640 pounds of halibut against the vessel's trip limit of 500 pounds, and nine fish below the minimum size of 32 inches, the smallest measuring 27 inches. The master attributed the overage to a miscalibrated deck scale, producing at the boarding a calibration certificate expired fourteen months. The Division's schedule rates the overage a class two violation and the undersized fish class three, aggravated by the expired certificate. Under the stipulated settlement, accepted to avoid hearing, the respondent: pays 3,400 dollars, of which 1,900 dollars is suspended for two years conditioned on no further violations; forfeits the proceeds of the overage, computed at 940 dollars at the dockside price of the day; and submits to scale verification at each offload for six months, at the respondent's expense of 60 dollars per verification. The undersized fish were seized at boarding and donated per protocol to the Harbor Mission kitchen. The vessel's permit history shows one prior warning, for late reporting, in the season before last. The settlement takes effect on countersignature by the regional director.
question: How many pounds of halibut were found aboard at the boarding?

passage: Application for museum accreditation, the Pump House Museum of Waterworks History, submitted to the Museums Standards Council. The museum occupies the 1893 pumping station on Fluvial Road, houses a collection of 4,100 catalogued objects including the triple expansion engine known as Matilda, still steamed six days a year, and received 21,000 visitors last year against 14,000 three years ago, the rise following the opening of the children's splash gallery. Governance: a charitable trust of nine trustees; the application discloses that two trustee terms exceeded the governing document's nine year limit and were regularized by the March general meeting, minutes enclosed. Collections care: environmental monitoring in all four galleries since 2019, with the archive moved last year from the damp west store, a known deficiency in the previous application, to a converted meter room achieving 50 percent relative humidity within a tolerance of five points. Documentation backlog stands at 6 percent of the collection, against the council's threshold of 10 percent. Staffing: three paid posts and 74 registered volunteers, of whom 12 hold boiler attendance certificates for steaming days. The forward plan, adopted in January, commits to oral history recording with retired waterworks staff, eleven interviews complete. The museum requests assessment visit dates avoiding the October steaming weekend.
question: What is the name of the triple expansion engine?

passage: Franchise renewal application, Copper Kettle Popcorn Wagon, municipal vending franchise 7, submitted to the city clerk of Harlow Green. The franchise, created in 1921 and held by the applicant's family since 1963, permits one wagon on the courthouse square from April through December. The applicant, Dot Ferrier, reports gross receipts of 41,000 dollars, franchise fees paid of 2,050 dollars at the 5 percent rate, and compliance with the health department's mobile vendor code, evidenced by inspection scores of 98, 97, and 99 across the season's three visits. One incident is disclosed: on fair weekend a propane regulator failed the morning check and the wagon did not operate that day, the applicant electing not to use the spare pending its own test, a decision the fire marshal's letter, enclosed, commends. The application requests two changes to franchise terms: extension of evening hours from 9 p.m. to 10:30 p.m. on the twelve nights of the summer concert series, and permission to add a second kettle for cinnamon corn, which under the code requires an additional fire suppression canister, quoted at 380 dollars and already ordered. The clerk's standard renewal term is five years. Six letters of support accompany, including one from the courthouse custodian citing thirty years of swept kernels.

passage: Notification of clinical trial amendment, filed with the Research Oversight Board by the Delling Institute, protocol 44-A, a randomized trial of a walking program for adults over 65 recovering from hip fracture. The amendment, the third, makes two changes. First, the target enrollment falls from 240 to 180 participants, following the statistician's revised power calculation using the observed variance in the six minute walk distance at interim, which was lower than the assumption drawn from the literature; power at the revised size remains 0.85 for the prespecified difference of 40 meters. Second, the protocol adds a home visit arm for participants unable to travel to the two clinic sites, delivered by the same physiotherapists on a monthly schedule, with the visit arm capped at 60 participants and analyzed separately from the primary comparison. Recruitment stands at 141, with 96 having completed the six month assessment; withdrawal remains at 9 percent, below the 15 percent the original protocol allowed for. The board is asked to note one deviation, already reported by expedited notice: a participant assessed at seven months rather than six due to a scheduling error, retained in analysis per the statistical plan's window of plus or minus five weeks. Consent forms incorporating the home visit arm are enclosed at version 3.1.
question: What is the revised target enrollment for the trial?

passage: Objection to trademark registration, filed with the Registry of Marks, opposition 88-419, opponent the Old Anchor Brewery of Pelling, against application 66-2107 by Anchorline Coffee Roasters. The opponent, brewing under an anchor device since 1887 and holding registrations 4402 and 4403 for beers and taproom services, objects to the applicant's mark, a fouled anchor within a rope circle, for coffee and cafe services, on grounds of likely confusion. The opponent's evidence: a consumer survey of 400 respondents in the three towns where both trade, in which 22 percent attributed the applicant's sign to the brewery; twelve instances of misdirected correspondence, exhibited; and the parties' shared use of nautical blue and cream livery. The applicant answers that anchors are common to the seaboard's trade generally, citing nineteen anchor marks on the register in classes from insurance to ropework, and that beer and coffee are distinct trades with distinct channels. The examiner's preliminary view, issued to focus the hearing, considers the goods sufficiently distant but the livery and the towns' overlap troubling, and invites the parties to mediation on a coexistence agreement limiting the applicant's palette. The applicant has consented to mediation; the opponent's consent is awaited. The hearing, if needed, is listed for March 3.
question: What percentage of survey respondents attributed the applicant's sign to the brewery?

passage: Application for a house move permit, filed by Talley Structural Movers on behalf of the Orchard Street Preservation Trust. The applicant proposes to move the Quimby House, a two story timber framed dwelling of 1846 weighing an estimated 96 tons, from its present lot at 14 Orchard Street, where it faces demolition for the school expansion, to a prepared foundation at the corner of Weld and Vine, a route of 0.7 miles. The route survey identifies: 14 utility crossings, of which nine require line lifts coordinated with two utilities under the attached schedules; one bridge, the Vine Street culvert, rated for the combined load of 128 tons with the transporter, verified by the county engineer's letter; and the removal and same day replanting of one street tree, a linden at the Weld corner, supervised by the town arborist. The move is proposed for a Sunday beginning at 5 a.m., with rolling closures and completion estimated by 2 p.m. Insurance of 5 million dollars names the town. The house will travel with its chimney braced internally, the applicant having removed only the chimney's upper six feet, numbered and palletized for reconstruction. Police detail costs of 3,800 dollars are prepaid. The trust's fundraising covered the move's full price of 118,000 dollars.
question: How much does the Quimby House weigh, by the estimate in the application?

passage: Annual return of the Pelling Harbor Pilots Association to the Maritime Commission. The association's seven licensed pilots performed 1,214 acts of pilotage in the year: 611 inbound, 590 outbound, and 13 movements within the harbor, the last category chiefly the shifting of the cement carrier Gray Duchess between the anchorage and the silo berth. Traffic rose 6 percent on the prior year, driven by the grain terminal's record season. The association reports one incident under rule 30: on February 8 the bulk carrier Andas Wind touched bottom at the turn of buoy 9 while under pilotage in fog, without damage found on survey and without pollution; the commission's inquiry, concluded in June, attributed the touching to an uncharted shoal deposited by winter storms and exonerated the pilot, and the association notes the shoal was dredged in May and the buoy repositioned 60 yards south. Pilot boat operations: the launch Curlew ran 2,900 engine hours, and her replacement, building at the Fenn yard for delivery next autumn at a contract price of 1.9 million dollars, will carry the name Curlew II by vote of the membership. Two apprentices continue in training, with one expected to sit the licensing examination in the spring. Tariff revision is not sought this year.
question: How many acts of pilotage did the pilots perform in the year?
